title: Many ectopic eye spots but one eye reflect competing goals of neighbouring cell groups

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Many ectopic eye spots but one eye reflect competing goals of neighbouring cell groups

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In Xenopus embryos injected with a potassium channel, many ectopic eye spots appear early but typically only one new eye forms; Levin interprets this as bidirectional signalling between channel-induced cells pushed toward an eye setpoint, which recruit neighbours, and uninjected neighbours whose setpoint is still 'gut', which signal to maintain normal fate.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2025, The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine › Bioelectricity as the Interface to Multicellularity › Applications: Modulating Endogenous Bioelectric Cues

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: At early stages in embryos injected with the potassium channel, many ectopic eye spots are detected, but just one new eye tends to appear at the end. This is the consequence of conversation between morphogenetic agents with different goals.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine”, BioEssays : news and reviews in molecular, cellular and developmental biology (2025), doi:10.1002/bies.202400196; section “Bioelectricity as the Interface to Multicellularity › Applications: Modulating Endogenous Bioelectric Cues”. Scope: Xenopus laevis embryos misexpressing potassium channels

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2025-wisdom-11: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.42

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The early-many-to-late-one pattern can be measured from existing experiments, but the proposed conversation between opposing setpoints requires new temporal and causal signalling data. Public endpoint phenotypes do not discriminate competition from differential survival or induction.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Track each induced eye field and its injected and uninjected neighbours over time while perturbing candidate bidirectional signals. Selective persistence or regression predicted by neighbour state, abolished by signal blockade, would support the competition mechanism.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Endpoint counts cannot establish bidirectional competition.

The mediating signals are explicitly unidentified.

Lineage-resolved longitudinal data are needed.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The numerical pattern, many early spots and usually one later eye, would be checkable if the counts were public, and they are not. Even those counts would not discriminate competing morphogenetic goals from ordinary neighbor competition, because both predict pruning of extra foci. The mechanism as stated needs new measurements of the proposed bidirectional signals.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Count ectopic eye spots per embryo over stages in channel-injected Xenopus, and record whether final eye number is one. A spot-count trajectory alone cannot separate competing setpoints from lateral inhibition unless signalling between injected and uninjected neighbors is also measured in both directions.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A decline from many spots to one eye is also predicted by competition and lateral inhibition without goals.

Bidirectional signalling between eye-biased and gut-biased cells was not deposited as a measurement.

Stage-wise spot counts are not a public dataset.
